paragraphs: Friend, here's what these last words teach me. David doesn't end his life bragging about his crown or his army. He says, "The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue" (2 Samuel 23:2). The last thing the king wants you to hear is not his own wisdom, it's God's.

And what does God's word say a good ruler looks like? Someone who rules "with justice," "in the fear of God," and God says that kind of ruler is like "the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn" (2 Samuel 23:3-4). Friend, that is NOT a picture of a loud, scary boss. It's a picture of something warm that makes everything around it grow. If you lead anybody at all, at work, at home, in a group chat that got out of hand, that's the kind of light God is asking for.

Then David leans on the promise: "He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part" (2 Samuel 23:5). He rests on what God said, and that is why he can end his days steady. The worthless, on the other hand, are like thorns, and thorns end in fire (2 Samuel 23:6-7). So, baker, let God's word be on your tongue, let His light shape how you treat people, and rest your whole hope in His promise, because after all those years in the dark, I can tell you His promises hold.
